borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The front extension, by reason of design, would present a discordant and fragmented feature which fails to integrate as with the established architectural rhythm of the dwelling or the wider street scene. The proposal is therefore considered contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies D4  of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP2,  DMD1, and DMD5 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposed development fails to demonstrate that adequate and independently accessible off‑street parking can be provided for three private vehicles within the site. The plans fail to set out the existing or proposed parking arrangements, nor do they evidence how three off‑street spaces could operate in practice given the current dropped kerb arrangement. In the absence of such information, and without the submission of a Parking Stress Survey, it has not been demonstrated that the proposal would avoid inaccessible parking spaces or increased on‑street parking demand. The development is therefore considered likely to result in increased parking stress and highway obstruction to the detriment of the free flow of traffic and highway safety, contrary to:National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024) Policies T1, T6 and T6.1 of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies DMT1 and DMT2 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan (September 2024)

The proposed development would result in the loss of a family-sized dwellinghouse, the need for which is clearly demonstrated in the development plan and supporting evidence base. While it would provide a dwelling in the form of an HMO, it fails to demonstrate that this meets an identified need. Additionally, the development site is not located within an area of high access to public transport and is therefore not considered an appropriate location for an HMO. As such, the proposal is considered to have a detrimental impact on the borough's housing supply and is contrary to the following policies:&nbsp;National Planning Policy Framework (MHCLG, December 2024)Policies D14 and T4&nbsp;of the London Plan (March 2021)Policies SP3, SP8, DMD1, DMT1 and DMH5 of the Barking and Dagenham Local Plan&nbsp;(September 2024)
description: Change of use of the dwelling (C3) to a 5no. bed, 5no. person HMO (C4), conversion of the garage including the construction of a single storey front extension, and installation of one window to the ground floor side elevation.
